per_document_scratch_directory.instrument_note: sweep3.py's own printed '%d files' figure is len(touched) -- files that had at least one non-protected edit -- NOT a count of files scanned/loaded by rglob. This disagrees with this plan's own CONTEXT.md/action-text assumption that a zero-edit document would still print '1 file'. The measured value wins per this plan's own instruction; the disagreement is recorded here and repeated in the SUMMARY. Non-vacuity (proof the scratch-directory instrument actually found and read the file, as opposed to the single-file-path bug where rglob finds nothing) is independently established two ways below: (a) a direct filesystem count of the .md file present under the scratch root, and (b) sweep3.py's own non-zero 'protected' counts, which are only possible if it read and tokenized lines from the file.

line_endings.note: D-35 leaves .gitattributes unchanged. This reading is recorded so a later executor does not 'fix' a line ending and produce a whole-file diff. Git's core.autocrlf=true means the working-tree copy is CRLF while the git object blob is normalized LF; Write-tool edits to these files in this phase will trigger git's own 'LF will be replaced by CRLF' notice on add/commit, which is expected and not an error.
